label: input token n at original positions 0-2
explanation: Fires only when the input is the letter n during the first three original-phase steps (t = 0, 1, 2), with about a quarter of such steps active and precision 1.0 on dev. It does not fire on n at original positions 3 or later, on any other token, or at the delimiter. In the copy phase it fires only very weakly and rarely (62 dev steps, mostly L = 3 sequences re-inputting n at t = 5). Magnitude depends on position: t = 1 has the largest mean activation, then t = 2, then t = 0. Its top activations (1.57) are all n at t = 1 right after i.

issues: Factual error in the explanation: it says 'About 25% of those steps are active', but that 25% is the active rate over ALL steps where n is the input (49372/197316). Nearly every step where n is the input at t<=2 is active: precision is 1.0 with 0 false positives on test, and n_predicted (49309) is about equal to n_active among those steps. So the feature fires on essentially every n at t=0-2, not a quarter of them. The predicate and label are unaffected.

Misses (test: 71 steps, 0.0% of activation mass) are one systematic but negligible class. They are copy-phase t=5 in L=3 sequences where n was at original position 1 and is now fed back, with weak activations of 0.03-0.18 of max. This matches the explanation's copy-phase note. Dev has 62 such steps and 1 stray step at t=3.

Other claims check out. The feature never fires at the delimiter or on any other token. Activation-mass shares by t are 0.448 (t=1), 0.322 (t=2) and 0.230 (t=0), with roughly equal active counts, so magnitude ranks t=1 > t=2 > t=0. The top activations (1.570) are all 'i n' at t=1.
Test scores reproduce: precision 1.0, recall 0.9986, F1 0.9993, mass recall 0.99985.
